Our new colleague helps with telephone support requests.
A teammate asks what the newest colleague does. Explain that this colleague helps with requests received by phone.
Onze agrees with singular de collega; nieuwe describes a recently joined colleague, not necessarily an unfamiliar person.
T=Na de introductie|V=ken|S=ik|O=de namen van mijn teamleden.
After the introduction, I know my team members' names.
You have finished a team introduction. Tell a colleague that you now know your team members' names.
Na de introductie is one first constituent. Kennen expresses familiarity with the names, rather than weten plus a fact clause.
Who guides the interns on the service desk?
New interns are joining the service desk. Ask a colleague which person is responsible for guiding them.
Wie is the subject of this question. There is no additional subject after begeleidt; de stagiairs is its object.
I used to work in a support team.
While introducing your experience to a new colleague, explain that you worked in a support team in the past.
Heb gewerkt reports past work experience; vroeger establishes that it belongs to an earlier period.
My colleague manages the user accounts.
Someone asks who manages user accounts. Explain that a colleague of yours performs that task.
Mijn is possessive; gebruikersaccounts is a plural compound whose singular is het gebruikersaccount.
We are getting to know the new team members.
A colleague asks how the team introductions are going. Say that you are getting to know the new team members together.
Leren kennen is a fixed combination meaning become acquainted with; kennen is a bare infinitive here.
S=Ik|V=ben|NEG=nog niet|C=bekend met onze interne werkwijze.
I am not yet familiar with our internal way of working.
You recently joined the team. Explain to a colleague that you are not yet familiar with its internal way of working.
Bekend met expresses familiarity; nog niet leaves open that you will become familiar later. Onze belongs with de werkwijze.
I will introduce myself during the team meeting.
Before your first team meeting, tell a colleague that you will introduce yourself during it.
Zich voorstellen is reflexive. Ik takes me; voorstellen stays joined as a final infinitive after zal.
MOD=Kan|S=ik|T=op mijn eerste werkdag|PP=met een collega|I=meelopen?
Can I shadow a colleague on my first working day?
You are arranging your first working day. Ask whether you can shadow a colleague while learning the job.
Meelopen is workplace shadowing here, not taking over the colleague's responsibilities. Op introduces the working day.
Yesterday the team leader introduced me to the colleagues.
A friend asks about yesterday's onboarding. Report that the team leader introduced you to your colleagues.
Gisteren is one first constituent; stelde follows before the subject. Mij is the introduced person, not the person doing the introduction.
Do you also work in the support team?
During a formal introduction to someone you do not know, politely ask whether they also work in the support team.
Formal u keeps werkt in inversion; the drop-t rule with subject je does not apply to u.
Introduce yourself to the new team members.
You are helping a colleague join a group of new team members. Ask that colleague informally to introduce themselves.
The addressed subject is understood; je is reflexive. Stel ... voor is the split form of voorstellen.
Where is the printer for visitors?
A visitor needs to print a document. Ask a colleague where the visitor printer is located.
Staat describes a standing device's location; de printer is the subject, not an object.
Is the quiet workspace available today?
You need a quiet place to work today. Ask whether the quiet workspace is available.
Beschikbaar expresses availability, not permission to access every room. Vandaag fixes the relevant day.
The meeting room is next to reception.
A new colleague asks where the meeting room is. Explain that it is located next to reception.
Zich bevinden is a reflexive location expression; singular de vergaderzaal takes zich.
May I use this available workstation?
You see an available workstation but do not know whether you may use it. Ask a colleague for permission.
Vrij describes that the workstation is unoccupied; mag asks separately for permission. Werkplek is a de-word, so deze fits.
L=Bij de ingang|V=staat|S=een kast voor bezoekerspassen.
There is a cabinet for visitor passes by the entrance.
A colleague is looking for visitor passes. Tell them where the cabinet for those passes stands.
A location phrase is first, followed by staat and the introduced subject een kast. No extra er is required in this location-first sentence.
This morning I looked for a quiet meeting room.
You are telling a colleague about this morning. Explain that you looked for a quiet meeting room then.
Zocht is simple past; zoeken naar introduces what you are looking for. Een rustige takes -e with de vergaderzaal.
Ask the receptionist for a visitor pass.
A visitor needs an entry pass. Tell a colleague to ask the receptionist for a visitor pass.
Vragen naar requests the item here. The instruction is addressed to the colleague, not to the receptionist directly.
I have already found the room for the video call.
A colleague offers to help you find the room for a video call. Explain that you have already found it.
Al means already; the completed search has a present result. Voor het videogesprek identifies the intended room.
I do not know which entrance visitors use.
You are arranging a visitor's arrival. Tell a colleague that you do not know which entrance the visitors use.
The embedded question begins with welke ingang; its subject de bezoekers precedes final gebruiken. Weten introduces missing factual information.
The lockers are opposite the staff entrance.
A colleague wants to store a bag before work. Explain where the lockers are located.
Plural de lockers takes staan. Tegenover is a location preposition meaning opposite.
I will show the new employee around the building.
Your team leader asks who will give a new employee a tour. Offer a firm commitment to show them around the building.
The employee is the object being shown around. Rondleiden remains joined after zal; the tour has not happened yet.
V=Heeft|S=deze werkplek|O=een aansluiting voor mijn laptop?
Does this workstation have a connection for my laptop?
You are choosing a workstation for your laptop. Ask whether this workstation has a suitable connection.
Heeft agrees with singular deze werkplek. The question concerns an available connection, not permission to connect an unauthorised device.
S=Ik|V=ben|T=tot de middag|C=bereikbaar via de servicedesk.
I am reachable through the service desk until noon.
A colleague asks how to contact you this morning. Explain that the service desk can reach you until noon.
Tot gives the end of availability; bereikbaar means contactable, not necessarily free of other tasks.
After my appointment, I can pick up support requests again.
You have an appointment during working hours. Tell a colleague when you will be able to resume handling support requests.
The complete appointment phrase is first; kan follows before ik. Weer means resuming an activity, not a new request.
V=Bent|S=u|T=na de middag|C=bereikbaar voor een kort gesprek?
Are you reachable for a short conversation in the afternoon?
You are arranging a formal conversation with someone you do not know. Politely ask whether they are reachable in the afternoon.
Formal u takes bent in this question. Na de middag is common Belgian wording for the afternoon.
I am not available for phone calls during the training.
You will attend training and cannot take calls during it. Explain this availability limit to your team.
Niet negates availability for calls during a particular period; it does not say you are absent for the entire day.
I have informed the scheduling team of my absence.
A colleague asks whether scheduling knows you will be absent. Say that you have already informed that team.
De planning can refer to the scheduling function/team here. Doorgegeven is the separable participle of doorgeven.
Can you take over my phone calls until ten o'clock?
You have a short morning commitment. Ask a colleague informally to handle your phone calls until ten.
The requested coverage ends at ten; it is not an indefinite transfer of responsibility. Overnemen remains a final infinitive.
I will let you know as soon as I am available again.
You cannot help a colleague immediately. Promise to notify them as soon as you become available again.
Laten weten takes a bare infinitive. Zodra introduces a future time clause whose finite ben is final; it does not use an extra zal.
T=Tijdens het eerste telefoontje|PAST=was|S=ik|C=al in een ander gesprek.
During the first call I was already on another call.
A colleague asks why you could not answer the first call earlier. Explain that you were already talking to someone else.
Was locates the conflicting call in the past. Al means that the other call had begun by that time.
S=Mijn werkdag|V=begint|T=een halfuur later dan die van jou.
My working day starts half an hour later than yours.
You compare schedules with a colleague. Explain that your working day begins half an hour later than theirs.
Later dan is a comparative. Die van jou refers back to de werkdag and avoids repeating the noun.
Let's coordinate our availability for tomorrow.
You and a colleague need to cover tomorrow's requests. Suggest coordinating when each of you is available.
A joint proposal includes the speaker. Onze belongs with de beschikbaarheid; the proposal is not a claim that schedules already agree.
I will come in earlier to support the morning shift.
Tomorrow's morning shift needs help. Explain to your colleague that you will come in earlier for that purpose.
A present with this arranged future context describes your plan. Om introduces purpose; ondersteunen has te here, unlike after a modal.
Who is the point of contact for urgent requests this evening?
Before the evening coverage begins, ask your team who the point of contact for urgent requests will be.
Wie is the subject. Dringende takes -e before plural meldingen; the question is limited to this evening.
I will take my break after the current call.
A colleague asks when you will take a break. Explain that you will finish the current call first.
The present plus a future sequence expresses an arrangement. Huidige identifies the call currently underway.
MOD=Kun|S=je|O=de telefoon|I=opnemen|G=terwijl ik even pauze neem?
Can you answer the phone while I take a short break?
You need a short break but calls must still be answered. Ask a colleague informally to cover the phone during your break.
Opnemen means answer the phone here. Terwijl introduces simultaneous actions; neem is final inside that clause.
We do not have a shared lunch break on busy days.
A new colleague asks about lunch arrangements. Explain that on busy days the team does not take lunch together.
Geen negates the indefinite shared lunch break. The qualification op drukke dagen matters; this is not a claim about every day.
The service desk remains reachable during my break.
A colleague worries that callers cannot reach support while you take a break. Explain that the service desk remains reachable.
Blijft expresses continuation; the team's coverage is not the same as your individual availability.
I have agreed on a later break time with my colleague.
Your team leader asks how your break is covered. Explain that you and a colleague have agreed on a later time for your break.
Afspreken met identifies the colleague; een later pauzemoment is the agreed item, not a completed break.
Let me know when you are back.
A colleague is about to take a break. Ask them informally to let you know when they return.
Me is the receiver of the information. Wanneer je terug bent describes a future return, with final bent.
During lunch we discussed the first working week.
You are telling a colleague about an earlier lunch. Say that you discussed the first working week together.
Bespraken agrees with plural we. Bespreken takes the topic as a direct object without over.
S=Een korte wandeling|V=helpt|O=me|TE=om daarna weer geconcentreerd te werken.
A short walk helps me work with concentration again afterward.
A colleague asks why you go outside during a break. Explain that a short walk helps you concentrate on work afterward.
Me is the person helped; the om te phrase describes the helpful result. Daarna means after the walk.
Are you taking the first break today?
You are checking today's coverage with a colleague. Ask informally whether they are taking the first break.
Neem before subject jij has no -t. De eerste pauze identifies its order rather than the duration.
I will include the new colleague at lunch.
A team member worries that the newcomer may feel left out. Promise to include the new colleague at lunch.
Iemand bij iets betrekken means include someone in something; it does not mean ask them to perform a task.
S=Ik|V=weet|NEG=niet|G=of de kantine vandaag open is.
I do not know whether the canteen is open today.
A colleague asks about lunch in the canteen. Say that you do not know whether it is open today.
Of means whether, not or, in this embedded yes/no question. Is is final in the subordinate clause.
Our break room is smaller than the canteen.
A new colleague asks about the eating areas. Explain that your team's break room is smaller than the canteen.
Onze accompanies de pauzeruimte; kleiner dan compares sizes. Klein describes the room, not the team.
I mainly manage accounts and access rights.
A colleague asks about your regular responsibilities. Explain that most of your administration concerns accounts and access rights.
Vooral limits the emphasis without claiming these are your only tasks. Accounts and toegangsrechten are direct objects.
I do not know this application well yet.
A colleague asks you to help with an application you are still learning. Explain that you are not very familiar with it yet.
Kennen concerns familiarity with the application. Nog niet goed does not necessarily mean you have never used it.
I have previously supported users remotely.
During an introduction, a teammate asks about your experience. Say that you have supported users remotely before.
Ondersteund has no added ge- with onder-. Eerder indicates previous experience without naming an exact date.
I want to get to know our cloud environment better.
You are discussing learning goals with a colleague. Explain that you want to become more familiar with the team's cloud environment.
This is a learning intention, not demonstrated competence. Leren kennen means become familiar with.
I feel confident with straightforward support questions.
Your mentor asks how confident you feel. Explain that straightforward support questions are within your comfort zone.
Voel is a verb; gevoel is a noun. Me is required for the state expression ik voel me zeker.
Q=Welke taken|V=horen|PP=bij mijn rol als junior beheerder?
Which tasks belong to my role as a junior administrator?
You are clarifying the boundaries of your new role. Ask your manager which tasks are part of your junior administrator position.
Horen bij is a fixed combination meaning belong to; it does not describe hearing a sound here.
S=Mijn vorige team|PAST=werkte|PP=met een ander meldingssysteem.
My previous team worked with a different ticketing system.
A colleague notices you are learning the request system. Explain that your previous team used a different system.
Vorige establishes an earlier team. Ander means different, not necessarily new or unknown.
I still have little experience with it.
Your mentor asks about a tool you have just discussed. Explain that you still have little experience using that tool.
Er ... mee refers back to the tool. Met changes to mee in this referring combination; er is not a location word.
S=Ik|V=weet|G=hoe het team de documentatie bijwerkt.
I know how the team updates the documentation.
A colleague asks whether you understand the team's documentation process. Say that you know how the team updates it.
Weten hoe introduces procedural factual knowledge. Bijwerkt stays joined at the end of the embedded clause.
I will go through the server documentation this week.
You are agreeing on onboarding work with your mentor. Commit to reviewing the server documentation this week.
Doornemen means review/read through here, not change the documentation. Deze week gives a time frame, not a completed result.
S=Ik|V=maak|O=aantekeningen|TE=om de werkwijze beter te onthouden.
I take notes to remember the procedure better.
A colleague asks why you are writing during a demonstration. Explain that you take notes to remember the procedure better.
Om names the purpose. Onthouden is remember/retain, while kennen is familiarity and weten concerns facts.
May I carry out this task under supervision?
You are not yet ready to perform a task alone. Ask your mentor for permission to carry it out with supervision.
Mag requests permission, not a claim of ability. Onder begeleiding explicitly limits how you would perform the task.
I work from home on Fridays.
A teammate asks about your regular Friday work location. Explain that you work from home that day.
Van thuis uit is common standard Belgian wording; vanuit huis is also used. Op vrijdag describes a recurring schedule here.
Tomorrow I will only be reachable through chat.
You are arranging tomorrow's contact options. Tell a colleague that chat will be the only way to reach you.
Alleen limits the contact channel. It does not mean that you will be working alone.
S=Ik|V=kom|L=naar kantoor|G=als de gebruiker mijn hulp ter plaatse nodig heeft.
I will come to the office if the user needs my help on site.
You are working remotely and discussing an unresolved request. Explain the condition under which you will come to the office.
Als introduces a condition, not a certainty. Nodig heeft forms the need expression at the end of the subordinate clause.
S=Ik|AUX=heb|O=een rustige plek voor de ondersteuningsgesprekken|PT=ingericht.
I have set up a quiet place for the support calls.
A colleague asks whether you can take support calls while working remotely. Explain that you have set up a quiet place for them.
Ingericht is the separable participle of inrichten. The statement concerns a completed setup, not a plan.
V=Ben|S=je|T=tijdens je thuiswerkdag|C=op hetzelfde nummer bereikbaar?
Are you reachable on the same number during your work-from-home day?
A colleague will work from home tomorrow. Ask informally whether the usual number will still reach them during that day.
Bereikbaar op een nummer is the fixed contact expression. Je before thuiswerkdag is possessive, while the earlier je is subject.
We can also discuss the handover remotely.
You and a colleague cannot meet at the office for a handover. Offer remote discussion as another possible option.
Kunnen expresses an available option here, not formal permission. Ook adds an option without claiming remote handover has already happened.
I do not have access to the office printer from home.
While working from home, you are asked to print a document on the office printer. Explain that you do not have access to it there.
Geen negates access as an uncountable noun. Tot introduces the resource; this does not by itself diagnose the technical cause.
Yesterday we worked from different offices.
A colleague asks where the team worked yesterday. Report that team members were working from different offices.
Werkten is plural past. Verschillende does not mean unknown; it describes more than one distinct office location.
Let's coordinate our office days with each other.
You and a teammate want to overlap at the office. Suggest coordinating the days on which you each come in.
Afstemmen op elkaar expresses reciprocal coordination. Onze agrees with plural kantoordagen.
I am setting up the workspace at home.
A colleague asks what you are doing at the moment. Explain that you are currently setting up your home workspace.
Aan het inrichten describes an action in progress. It does not mean the workspace is ready yet.
Which conversations do we prefer to have at the office?
Your team is agreeing how to work together remotely. Ask which conversations the group would rather hold at the office.
Een gesprek voeren is a fixed expression. Liever expresses a preference, not a ban on remote conversations.
S=Ik|V=gebruik|O=een headset|TE=om thuis duidelijk verstaanbaar te zijn.
I use a headset so that I can be heard clearly at home.
Someone asks about your remote-call setup. Explain that you use a headset to make yourself clearly audible while at home.
Verstaanbaar concerns whether others can hear/understand the speech clearly, not whether the message's content has been understood.
